strategy_title: Shrinking Tile Sizes to Reduce Register Pressure Backfires
strategy_description: Reducing BLOCK_M×BLOCK_N tile sizes (e.g. from 256×128 to 64×64 or smaller) to lower register usage and improve occupancy can severely worsen performance when the kernel has significant shared memory bank conflicts. In this case, occupancy improved from 12.5% to 37.5% and registers dropped from 254 to 80 per thread, but Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction exploded from 4.6 to 33.0 cycles and Mem Busy jumped from 60% to 95.5%, indicating that smaller tiles dramatically increased the ratio of shared memory accesses per output element, amplifying bank conflicts (from 5.3-way to 17.0-way average) and MIO pipeline pressure. The net effect was a 3.4× slowdown: the occupancy gain was completely overwhelmed by the increased per-element shared memory traffic and bank conflict stalls.
applicable_when: Kernel has very high register usage (>200 registers/thread) causing occupancy <15%, AND shared memory bank conflicts are low (<5-way average), AND the bottleneck is truly register-limited occupancy rather than memory access pattern.
do_not_apply_when: The kernel already has significant shared memory bank conflicts (>5-way average, UncoalescedSharedAccess speedup_pct >30%). Smaller tiles increase the number of shared memory load/store operations per output element, amplifying bank conflicts and MIO pipeline pressure far more than the occupancy gain can compensate. Also avoid when Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction is already low (<6), indicating the existing tile size is efficiently hiding latency.
framework_notes: Triton autotune config changes only affect tile sizes and software pipelining (num_stages). The bank conflict amplification from smaller tiles is a fundamental issue: with GEMM-style kernels that use shared memory staging, smaller BLOCK_K means more K-loop iterations and proportionally more shared memory accesses per output element. The MIO pipeline saturation (CPIStall rules appearing after the change) is the direct consequence.

Each sub-group dot has bounded TF32 error proportional to BLOCK_K (not total K=576), keeping max_diff within atol=1e-3. This routes computation through Tensor Cores while preserving correctness. Tensor Core utilization will also reduce register pressure (Triton allocates fewer registers for TC-based matmul vs scalar FFMA), improving occupancy from 12.5% toward 25-50%.

strategy_title: K-Decode Reorder for Weight Coalescing Backfires
strategy_description: Reordering the K-dimension decode in a Triton convolution kernel to align the fastest-varying k-offset with the weight tensor's stride-1 dimension (kw) did not improve performance; instead it caused a 3.4× slowdown. The change was confounded by the autotuner simultaneously selecting much smaller tile sizes (BLOCK_M×BLOCK_N dropped from 256×64 to 64×64 or smaller), which dramatically increased shared memory traffic per output element and worsened bank conflicts from 5.3-way to 17.0-way average, causing Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction to explode from 4.6 to 30.5 and Mem Busy to saturate at 95%. The K-decode reorder itself cannot be evaluated in isolation because the autotuner config space changed simultaneously, making it impossible to attribute the regression to the decode order change versus the tile size reduction.
slow_pseudocode:
# AFTER (regressed): small tiles + reordered K-decode
@triton.autotune(configs=[
    Config(BLOCK_M=32, BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=16, stages=3, warps=2),
    Config(BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=16, stages=3, warps=4),
    # ... all BLOCK_M×BLOCK_N <= 4096
])
def conv_epilogue_kernel(...):
    offs_k = k_off + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
    # Reordered: kw innermost (stride=1 in W memory)
    kw = offs_k % KW
    kh = (offs_k // KW) % KH
    in_c = offs_k // (KH * KW)
    # 17-way bank conflicts, Warp Cycles/Inst = 30.5, Duration = 56.4ms
fast_pseudocode:
# BEFORE (baseline): large tiles + original K-decode
@triton.autotune(configs=[
    Config(BLOCK_M=256, BLOCK_N=64,  BLOCK_K=16, stages=2, warps=4),
    Config(BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=16, stages=2, warps=8),
    # ... BLOCK_M×BLOCK_N up to 32768
])
def conv_epilogue_kernel(...):
    offs_k = k_off + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
    # Original: in_c innermost
    in_c = offs_k % IN_C
    kh = (offs_k // IN_C) % KH
    kw = offs_k // (IN_C * KH)
    # 5.3-way bank conflicts, Warp Cycles/Inst = 4.6, Duration = 16.7ms
applicable_when: Never apply this specific combination: K-decode reorder paired with simultaneous autotuner config space reduction to smaller tiles. If testing K-decode reorder, hold tile sizes constant to isolate the effect.
do_not_apply_when: When the autotuner config space is changed simultaneously with the K-decode reorder — the two changes interact destructively. The tile size reduction dominates and amplifies shared memory bank conflicts far beyond any coalescing benefit from the decode reorder. Also do not apply when the kernel already has significant bank conflicts (>5-way) that are tile-size-sensitive.
framework_notes: The Triton autotuner selected smaller tiles from the new config space (BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64 vs prior BLOCK_M=256, BLOCK_N=64), which is the same confound seen in iteration 1. Any future K-decode reorder experiment must keep the autotuner config space identical to the baseline to isolate the decode order effect.
